blocks.content: While CACP recommends the Minimum Support Price (MSP) to safeguard farmers, FCI executes the procurement, storage, and distribution of foodgrains across the nation.

rows: Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
Recommends MSP for crops and FRP for sugarcane
Procurement, storage, buffer stocking, and distribution of foodgrains

items: CACP recommendations for MSP are purely advisory in nature and not legally binding on the Government of India.
FCI is a statutory body, whereas CACP is an attached office under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
Always note the distinct ministries: CACP belongs to Ministry of Agriculture, while FCI operates under Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: CACP is an advisory body that recommends Minimum Support Prices (MSP), whereas FCI is an executive statutory body responsible for procurement, storage, and distribution.
CACP functions under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, while FCI operates under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution.
FCI was established under the Food Corporations Act, 1964, to implement the national food policy.
CACP recommends MSPs for 22 mandated agricultural crops and Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) for sugarcane.
